gtk.title: Pushchairs and buggies
gtk.text: There’s no rule against pushchairs on the promenade, and there are ramps and dropped kerbs along Oystermouth Road. In 2026 there were baby changing facilities and baby feeding areas by the information points at the Civic Centre and the Cenotaph.

gtk.title: Dogs
gtk.text: Dogs aren’t banned from the seafront, but the show advises against bringing them because of the aircraft noise and the crowds. I would leave yours at home, and only guide dogs are allowed in the Flight Deck.

gtk.title: Your own food and drink
gtk.text: BBQs aren’t allowed. I couldn’t find a rule on bringing your own food or alcohol onto the prom, so I would check the FAQs before you pack any drink. Alcohol can’t be taken into the Flight Deck, and in 2026 there were bars at the Civic Centre and near the Cenotaph.

gtk.title: Gazebos, windbreaks and chairs
gtk.text: I couldn’t find a rule on gazebos, windbreaks or chairs for the seafront. Low chairs or a blanket are what I would bring, and I would ask the show before you take a gazebo, as the prom gets tight.

gtk.title: Water refill points
gtk.text: In 2026 there were dedicated water stations where you could refill bottles. I would bring a refillable bottle and top it up before the flying starts.

gtk.title: Changing Places toilet
gtk.text: The Civic Centre Changing Places toilet is about 50 metres from the accessible viewing area there. There’s another at the Secret Bar and Café, about 250 metres from the Cenotaph viewing area.

gtk.title: Carers' tickets
gtk.text: The show is free, so there’s no carer ticket to sort out. In 2026 the two accessible viewing areas had folding chairs for companions if needed, first come first served.

gtk.title: Hearing support
gtk.text: I couldn’t find anything on hearing loops or BSL. If you rely on either, I would ring the show’s accessibility line on 01792 635428 before you go.

gtk.title: Quiet area
gtk.text: The Civic Centre viewing area is close to Swansea Library inside the building, which is somewhere quieter if the noise gets too much. In 2026 the National Autistic Society Swansea branch were at both accessible viewing areas to help families.

gtk.title: Re-entry
gtk.text: It’s a public seafront with no gates, so you can pop into town and come back. Just bear in mind the event car parks had no re-admittance in 2026.

gtk.title: First aid and lost children
gtk.text: St John Ambulance ran first aid points at the Civic Centre and on the prom near the Cenotaph in 2026. Lost children are taken to the information points in the same two places, so I would pick up a free Stay Safe wristband when you arrive.

gtk.title: If it rains
gtk.text: Unfortunately the weather on the day will be what it will be, so plan accordingly. If it’s fresh, dress in layers to keep warm. The Flight Deck has marquee cover if you’ve booked it.

days.html:
Pick Your Day

Swansea is two quite different days. In 2026 the Saturday had the longer flying programme and carried on into the night with Afterburn, while the Sunday started earlier and finished mid afternoon. If you can only make one, answer three quick questions and I’ll tell you which I would pick.

Saturday flying13:45 to about 17:30
Sunday flying12:26 to about 15:30
EveningAfterburn, Saturday
Ground displays10:00 to 18:00

Who’s coming?

What sounds best?

How long can you stay?

I Would Pick The Saturday

  1. WhyYou get the full daytime flying and Afterburn on the same day, and in 2026 that meant the Typhoon flew twice. The Apache and the Jet Pitts were Saturday only too.
  2. Good to knowIt’s a very long day. The ground displays close at 18:00, so I would suggest a proper break in town or on the beach before the evening show.
  3. Getting thereIn 2026 the Park and Ride ran 09:00 to 22:30 on the Saturday and the event car parks stayed open until 23:30. More in .

I Would Pick The Sunday

  1. WhyThe flying starts earlier and the last display in 2026 was the Typhoon at 15:18, so you can be heading home at a sensible time with little ones.
  2. Good to knowThere was a break of about an hour after 13:21 on the Sunday in 2026. If you aren’t waiting for a particular display, I would use it for lunch or a toilet break.
  3. Getting thereThe 2026 Park and Ride ran 08:30 to 20:00 on the Sunday. Try to arrive before the flying starts, as the roads get very busy.

I Would Pick The Saturday Evening

  1. WhyIf you’re more into the spectacle than the aircraft, Afterburn may work for you. In 2026 it had the Typhoon’s afterburners, the Firebirds, the Otto helicopter with pyrotechnics, then 200 drones and fireworks.
  2. Good to knowThe evening Flight Deck session sold out in 2026, so if you want a seat, I would book as soon as tickets go on sale.
  3. Getting thereExpect big queues after the fireworks. If you’re on the train, please check your last train before you set off.

The Two Days In 2026

SaturdayGround displays 10:00 to 18:00. Flying from the RAF Tutor at 13:45 to the Jet Pitts at 17:20, with the Typhoon at 16:48.
Saturday eveningAfterburn. The Typhoon at 20:55, the Firebirds at 21:18, the Otto helicopter at 21:36, then drones and fireworks at about 21:50.
SundayGround displays 10:00 to 18:00. Flying from the Starlings at 12:26, with the Typhoon closing the show at 15:18.
Jack’s tipIf Afterburn comes back in 2027 and you can only do one day, I would pick the Saturday and pace yourself. Twelve hours on a seafront is a lot for anyone, so think about how long your group can really manage. My shows how I would split it up.

Times are from the 2026 show. The 2027 dates and times haven’t been announced yet.

ground.html:
The Ground Show

The ground displays stretch from the Civic Centre down to Brynmill Lane, with even more along Oystermouth Road while it’s closed to traffic. They open at 10:00 and the flying doesn’t start until the afternoon, so you’ve got a good few hours. I would use them.

CostFree to wander
Open10:00 to 18:00 (2026)
WhereCivic Centre to Brynmill Lane
FunfairBy the Civic Centre

How I Would Do It

  1. Save your pitch firstIf you want a front row seat, head to the prom or the beach and set up your chairs or blanket before anything else. The crowd centre by the Cenotaph fills first.
  2. Then walk the ground displaysTake a look round the forces displays, speak to the crews, visit the trade stands and check the food options while someone minds your spot.
  3. Toilet before the flyingI would go before the first aircraft appears, as the queues build quickly once the flying starts.
  4. Use the breaksThe 2026 timetable had a half hour break on the Saturday and about an hour on the Sunday. If you aren’t waiting for a particular display, that’s your chance for a toilet or food break.

Things To See

Free

The Military Village

The armed services bring large combat vehicles, have a go activities and information trailers. If anyone in your group is thinking about joining up, this is a good place to ask questions.

Free

Army, Air And Sea Cadets

The cadets have interactive displays of the things they get up to. Children love to see what they could be doing in a few years.

Ask on the day

Simulators And VR

There are flight simulators and VR experiences where you can sit in the cockpit of a Red Arrow or a Typhoon. I would do these in the morning before the queues build.

Free

Meet The Display Teams

Many of the display teams come down to the ground, so you may get the chance to speak to the pilots. Keep an eye out for flying suits as you walk round.

Free

Static Aircraft

Static aircraft are part of the ground displays, but I haven’t seen which ones named, so I wouldn’t come expecting a big park of them. If one is opened up for you to take a look inside, it’s worth a peek, and some crews sell exclusive merch in or outside the aircraft.

Civic Centre

Funfair And Amusements

The funfair and amusements sit by the Civic Centre. It’s handy for a break if the little ones lose interest between displays.

Free

Live Music And Entertainers

Pop up busker spots, a few numbers from the military bands, and children’s entertainers along the prom.

Pay as you go

Food And Trade Stands

Food trucks and trade stands run along Oystermouth Road, the Cenotaph and the Civic Centre. I have put more on the food in .

Jack’s tipEar defenders aren’t handed out. Some traders may have them for sale, but I wouldn’t rely on it, so bring your own. Your child’s ears are delicate, so try to protect them as much as possible, especially for the Typhoon.

skipped.flights: I couldn't find any pleasure, helicopter, warbird or balloon flights offered at or from the show. It's a seafront show over the bay with no airfield, and none are mentioned on the official site.
skipped.support: The Wales Airshow is free and run by Swansea Council. The official site only asks businesses for sponsorship (Commercial@swansea.gov.uk). There are no public donation, bucket collection, programme or volunteer appeals; the volunteer cadets are supported by sponsors rather than recruited from the public.

notes: 1) The Key details box in the overview says 'Flying: From about 12:30 to 13:45'. That looks wrong. In 2026 the Saturday flying ran 13:45 to about 17:30 (Jet Pitts at 17:20) and the Sunday ran 12:26 to about 15:30 (Typhoon at 15:18). https://www.walesnationalairshow.com/wales-airshow-timetable/ 2) Right for you says 'Static aircraft: None advertised' and 'There's no static aircraft park'. The official ground displays page lists static aircraft among the ground attractions, although none are named. https://www.walesnationalairshow.com/ground-displays-2/ 3) Afterburn times differ between sources: the official Afterburn page says 20:30 to 21:45, Visit Swansea Bay says 20:50 to 22:00 (which the Help tab uses), and the timetable starts at 20:55 with drones and fireworks at 21:50. https://www.walesnationalairshow.com/afterburn/ 4) Help On Show Days, Running Out Of Water, still refers to three refill stations at the 2024 show. The 2026 FAQs say there are dedicated water stations to refill bottles. https://www.walesnationalairshow.com/information/faqs/ 5) Food and facilities, Accessibility, is written as 2025. The 2026 accessibility page has the same arrangements (two viewing areas at the Cenotaph and the Civic Centre, NAS Swansea branch, Changing Places at the Civic Centre and Secret Bar and Cafe), so it could be updated to 2026. https://www.walesnationalairshow.com/information/visitor-information/disabled-visitors/ 6) Not on the page yet but useful: the official site says some traders may sell ear defenders, there's a taxi drop off at the Brangwyn Hall layby, and Swansea Mobility Hire lends scooters and wheelchairs. 7) walesairshow.co.uk is now a parked domain, so make sure nothing links there; the official site is walesnationalairshow.com (the page already uses that). No 2027 date had been announced when I checked.
